text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Pakistan said it was ready to settle with indcia the issue of demilitarisation of the Siachen glacier in accordance with the Simla agreement.
- Ninety-four nomination papers were filed against 46 Senate (upper house) seats to be vacated by members whose term will end on March 20. Elections for Senate are set for March 16.
- India has agreed to resume talks with Pakistan at the level of senior officials later this month, the United News of India reported.

- The trial of Asif Ali Zardari, husband of opposition leader Benazir Bhutto, and six others accused in the killing of Bhutto's brother Murtaza, would take place inside the Landhi prison in Karachi, the Sindh provincial authorities said.
- M.S. Habib deputy chairman of Glaxo-Wellcome Pakistan Ltd, has recommended the import of pharmaceutical raw materials from India where the prices are lower compared to other markets.
- The government has earmarked Sui Nothern Gas Pipelines, Sui Southern Gas Company, Oil and Gas Development Corporation and Pakistan State Oil for privatisation in 1997.
- The state-run Ghee Corporation of Pakistan would auction 6,000 tonnes of palm oil and 1,000 tonnes of palmolein to the private secto.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has suspended 18 officials of Customs and Income Tax departments for violation of rules.
- For the first time in two decades, Sunday is a weekly holiday instead of Friday.
